hb_kingsrest_mouth.name: The Kings' Rest — Mouth
hb_kingsrest_mouth.desc: A slab door, sunk deep into the mound's northern face, sealed with age rather than any lock a smith would recognize. Cold air breathes out around its edges, carrying iron and older dust.

in.lockedMsg: The slab door will not give.
in.hint: force it (might), find its catch (wits), or use the Keeper's Key

onEnterOnce: Vell: "A dynasty predating the Hollow King's own line? Marrowgate's histories barely mention it. I have questions, and no one left alive to answer them."

actions.label: force the slab door (might)
fx: You put your whole weight into it. Centuries of settled earth break loose around the frame, and the slab grinds inward.
The slab does not move. Whatever seals it, strength alone is not enough.

actions.label: find the old release catch (wits)
fx: A catch-stone, worn smooth but still proud of the frame, gives under the right pressure in the right place. The slab swings in.
If there is a catch here, your fingers have not found it yet.

actions.label: open the door with the Keeper's Key
fx: The Keeper's Key turns something you cannot see. The slab door opens like it was only ever waiting to be asked properly.

actions.label: speak the old rest-formula (will)
fx: You don't ask it kindly. You speak the words a door like this was carved to hear regardless — let the road remember, let the door remember, and rest — and old dust sifts loose from the seal.
The words you have aren't the words it wants. The slab does not so much as shift.

actions.label: hang the bell at the mound's door
fx: You wire the bell above the slab door, unasked and unsanctioned. No Keeper blessed it. The wind finds it anyway, some nights, and it rings.

hb_kingsrest_hall.name: The Kings' Rest — Hall
hb_kingsrest_hall.desc: A long hall, cold enough to see your own breath. Old shields hang from the walls, rusted to lace. A grave-wight stands square in the passage deeper in, exactly where a guard would stand if a guard could not die.
hb_kingsrest_hall.brief: The cold hall. A grave-wight bars the way.

in.lockedMsg: The grave-wight bars the passage, patient as stone.
in.hint: defeat it, slip past it (grace), or face it down (will)

variants.brief: The cold hall. The passage stands open now.

actions.label: slip past it — a fail costs 1hp (grace)
fx: You keep to the wall's shadow and slip by while it is still turning. The passage in stands open.
It catches your sleeve on the way past. You wrench free, but not cleanly.

actions.label: stand fast and face it down (will)
fx: You do not step back. Whatever it was waiting four hundred years to see, your standing fast is apparently it — it steps aside.
It does not move, and neither, this time, does your nerve hold long enough to matter.

actions.label: show the Keeper's Key to the grave-wight
fx: The wight's blind stare finds the Key before you've raised it all the way. Whatever it was set to watch for, a Keeper's own trust isn't it. It steps aside, unhurried, and lets you through.

actions.label: pin it and demand the name it guards
fx: You don't slip past it or talk it down. You put it on the ground and hold it there until whatever's left of a mind in it gives up its post. 'Caelrin,' it manages, like the word costs it something.

hb_kingsrest_throne.name: The Kings' Rest — the Old Court
hb_kingsrest_throne.desc: The mound's heart: a ring of stone seats around a cold hearth-stone, and in the largest seat, the eldest of a dynasty older than the Hollow King's own line. He does not rise. He has had four hundred years to decide it is not worth it.
hb_kingsrest_throne.brief: The old court, and its eldest king.
onEnterOnce: Brother Osk: "Another grief nobody wrote a rite for in time. I keep finding these. I would like, someday, to stop finding these."

variants.name: The Old Court, at Rest
variants.desc: The stone seats stand empty now, the hearth-stone cold but no longer grieving. Whatever sat here has finally lain back down, and taken its silence with it.
The old court sits as it always has, but something in the room has eased — a debt paid, not forgiven. The eldest king inclines his head, once, and says nothing further.

variants.name: The Burned Court
variants.desc: Ash and collapsed stone where the ring of seats stood. Whatever kept this court sitting has been burned past rising again — past everything, if the old rites are believed.

actions.label: lay the Keeper's Key on the hearth-stone
fx: You set the Key on the cold hearth-stone. It turns no lock here — it does not need to. The eldest king recognizes it, and that recognition is enough. The old court lies down.

actions.label: return the queen's ring to the court
fx: You set the ring back where it came from. The eldest king takes it without a word, turns it once in fingers gone to bone, and inclines his head. Not forgiveness. It will do.
Lys: "A debt paid instead of a grave burned. That's a kind of ending I can live with."

actions.label: break the pitch-jar and fire the court
fx: The pitch catches fast, faster than pitch should. By the time you reach the mouth the ground itself is groaning. Behind you, the hearth-stone cracks clean in half.
Tamsin: "Quick. Ugly. Done. I won't pretend I mind an ending that doesn't argue with you."

actions.label: shatter the hearth-stone (might)
fx: You don't wait on pitch. You put your full weight into the cold hearth-stone until it cracks clean in half, and whatever was sitting this court out finally has nowhere left to sit.
The hearth-stone is older and harder than you are tonight. It doesn't so much as chip.

actions.label: speak the Great Rite over the court
fx: You speak the Rite whole, the way Wren taught it, needing no found verse and no borrowed key. The eldest king rises once, to bow to the office and not to you, before he lies back down for good.

actions.label: settle on the name Caelrin
fx: You settle on Caelrin. If the roll and the stone are honest with each other, it's him.

actions.label: settle on the name Roderic
fx: You settle on Roderic. It's the name everyone in Barrowmere already knows.

actions.label: settle on the name Ossian
fx: You settle on Ossian. Nothing you've found points to him either way — it would be a plain guess.

actions.label: speak the name — wrong costs you
fx: 'Caelrin.' The name lands like it was always going to. The eldest king closes his eyes, recognized at last by somebody other than himself. One by one, the old court lies back down.
Vell: "A name, restored. I didn't expect to feel this pleased about someone else's."
'Roderic.' The old court does not answer to it. Cold air moves behind you — the grave-wight you passed is not staying passed tonight.
'Ossian.' Nothing in the ring so much as stirs. Whatever you hoped for, it wasn't a silence this complete. Cold air moves behind you, unsettled.

actions.label: weigh what this grief asks
fx: Nothing here can be settled until the old court's grievance is heard — ask the eldest king what he wants.
The rest can be done outright: the Keeper's Key is yours — lay it on the hearth-stone.
You've settled on a name. Speak it, or change your mind first — wrong, and it costs the Keepers' trust, and the wight won't stay quiet.
The rest can also be earned by naming him true. The downs hold evidence, not verses; settle on a name, then speak it — wrong costs you.
The bargain stands ready: the queen's ring is yours — return it to the court.
The bargain wants the queen's ring — buy it, lift it, or labor for it, at the chandler's shop.
The burn stands ready: a jar of pitch is yours — break it here.
The burn wants a jar of pitch from the chandler's shop — or shatter the hearth-stone yourself (might), pitch or none.

hb_grave_wight.name: grave-wight
hb_grave_wight.desc: Old mail gone to rust over bone, standing an old post with nothing left to guard but habit. What's left of its grip does not care what you're wearing.
onDeath: The wight comes apart into rag and rust. The passage in stands open, whatever it cost you to open it.
It was already still, whatever kept it upright already settled.

hb_eldest_king.name: the eldest king
hb_eldest_king.desc: A king the shape of patience worn thin, sitting very still in the largest of the stone seats.

topics.label: who are you
topics.say: The eldest of the old court speaks first, in a voice like settling stone. 'Another one, come to gawk at kings the world forgot to finish burying.'

topics.label: what you want
topics.say: We ruled before the Hollow King's blood was crowned; his own line's founder robbed us of more than land. Name the eldest true, buy back what was taken, or burn us — we are done being merely remembered.

topics.label: the name even he has lost
topics.say: 'Ask it plainly, then.' A long pause. 'Say it back to me, if you can — I find I no longer can. His line was thorough. Find it in the ground, if you want it said true.'

topics.label: the Keeper's Key
topics.say: That key was cut for this door before your grandmother's grandmother learned to walk. Use it here, at the hearth-stone, and be done with it properly.

topics.label: the name in the downs
topics.say: Cut in stone at the causeway, rolled off in the ring-ditch, and the mere still answers if you ask it right. They do not all agree. That is the puzzle, not a flaw in it.

topics.label: step back from the hearth-stone
topics.say: We are not going anywhere. That has rather been the problem.

stages.text: You hold the Keeper's Key. Use it at the hearth-stone to rest the old court outright.
You've settled on a name. Speak it at the great mound's heart — a wrong one costs you.
You have a grave-good to return. Bring it to the hearth-stone to bargain the old court's rest.
You have pitch enough to burn the old court out for good, if that is the road you choose.
The grievance is heard. Find the Key, gather evidence to name him true, or bring a grave-good or pitch.
The great mound stands before you. Go in and hear the old court before deciding anything.
A hundred mounds ring Barrowmere, and one great mound above them all holds a court that will not lie down.
You have every piece. Settle on a name at the great mound, and speak it.
The evidence doesn't agree with itself yet. Settle on a name, or keep looking.
The eldest king has no name anyone living remembers. The causeway, the ring-ditch, and the mere might.
Force the Hall's old chest, pick its lock, or earn enough of Keeper Wren's trust to ask her outright.
Keeper Wren tends the ruined Hall alone. Hear what she has to say before asking for what she guards.
The Crown surveyor wants to know which mounds are worth digging. Tell him, or send him off with nothing.
A digger works the robbed mounds, out past the Toll Stones. Stop him or take your cut.

epilogue.text: The old court under the great mound lies down at last. Barrowmere sleeps through the night for the first time anyone there can remember.
The barrow-queen's ring went back into the ground. The old court is not rested, but it is quiet, and Barrowmere calls that enough.
Three mounds fell in the night the fire took the old court. Nothing under that ground grieves anymore. Nothing rests there either.
The great mound's door still stands at Barrowmere's edge, and the old court still sits up some nights, waiting on someone else.
The Crown's surveyor left Barrowmere with a full map and a light conscience. Diggers followed inside the season.
The Crown's surveyor left Barrowmere with an empty map. The warden still keeps the count Marrowgate never gets to see.
The Keepers' Hall gave up its ledger at last. What it says of a Marrowgate exile is not this telling's secret to keep.
The Keeper's Key left Barrowmere in a pocket, bound for a pilgrim stair at Coldpass that has not opened in a hundred years.
The Keeper's Key left Barrowmere in a pocket and turned the pilgrim stair at Coldpass, a hundred years after it last turned.
The eldest king had a name after all, one nobody living had spoken in four hundred years. Now one has.
Barrowmere still tells, half-admiring, of the wrong name once said to the old court before the right one came.

hb_warden_flask.name: a warden's flask
hb_warden_flask.hint: left for whoever goes in past the door, by old custom

fx: Barrow-mead, bitter with the iron shavings the old custom calls for. It steadies you more than the taste suggests.
